episode_title: 🎙️ Episode 17: From Side Hustle to Success 🚀🏡 With Jay Baysden ✨

real_qa.q: How did Jay Baysden start Baycom Computer and Networks as a side hustle?
real_qa.r: Jay joined the Navy in 1997 and got into the computer field. After getting out and working in IT at Fort Eustis, he needed extra spare money, so he took a real estate sign, stood it up in the back of his truck, and put 'computer repair' and his phone number on it. That's how Baycom started 19 years ago.
real_qa.requete: How did Jay Baysden start Baycom

real_qa.q: What is Jay Baysden's core business advice for entrepreneurs starting a new venture?
real_qa.r: Jay emphasizes doing your homework and researching your field and market thoroughly before investing heavily. He advises speaking to industry experts—such as an IT professional or real estate agent—to understand the technical and financial sides before committing significant capital. He warns that many entrepreneurs fail because they don't do enough research and simply 'throw a dart and see what sticks,' potentially losing up to $400,000 on an ill-informed business.
real_qa.requete: entrepreneur advice research before starting business

real_qa.q: What service transformation did Baycom Computer and Networks undergo?
real_qa.r: Baycom transitioned from a break-fix company model to a managed services model. This change allowed them to take phone calls remotely and handle service calls more efficiently, fundamentally shifting the type of business they operate.

real_qa.q: What book did Jay Baysden credit with changing his IT career?
real_qa.r: Jay credits the book 'Managed Services in a Month' by Carl Paula Chuck as the book that changed his career the most. He read it during Baycom's transition from a break-fix company to a managed services provider.
real_qa.requete: Managed Services in a Month Carl Paula Chuck

real_qa.q: What enterprise contract scale is Baycom Computer and Networks targeting next?
real_qa.r: Jay plans to pursue larger contracts in the range of $100,000 to $200,000 for cabling, wiring, and camera installation projects at a larger scale, moving beyond the smaller business clients they have historically served.

guest.bio_context: Jay comes from a long line of business owners—his father, grandfather, and great-grandfather. He joined the Navy in 1997 and entered the computer field, later working in IT at Fort Eustis before starting Baycom as a side hustle 19 years ago with a real estate sign and a truck. He has since grown the business into a brick-and-mortar operation with employees and vehicles serving York County and clients across the nation.

real_quote: Do your homework, do some research on your field on your market—the money's out there, all you gotta do is go get it.
